title: How The Great Train Robbery Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the 1963 Great Train Robbery in England: the Bowler Hat Gang and South Coast Raiders hijacked the Up Special mail train carrying about 2.6 million pounds from Glasgow to London, aided by an inside man (Ulsterman, later named as Patrick McKenna). They covered the red signal, beat conductor Jack Mills, forced a driver to move the train to Bridego Bridge, and hid at Leatherslade Farm, where Monopoly and ketchup left prints. Scotland Yard's Flying Squad (Tommy Butler) rounded up the gang, trials brought heavy sentences (Bigs, Goody, Cordrey, Bull), and Ronald Biggs escaped, living openly in Brazil. The episode closes with listener mail about horse milk (kumis) from Kazakhstan.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the Great Train Robbery
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Josh's cold and a planned trip to Vancouver, then introduce the 1963 Great Train Robbery and mention documentaries and films about it.

segments.title: Planning the heist and the Up Special
segments.summary: The hosts describe the origins of the plan, the Bowler Hat Gang and South Coast Raiders joining forces, and the Up Special mail train that ran nightly from Glasgow to London carrying bank money with little security.

segments.title: The inside man and the bank holiday timing
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the inside man code-named Ulsterman, identified as Patrick McKenna, and why the bank holiday timing meant a larger cash load on the train.

segments.title: Stopping the train and assaulting the conductor
segments.summary: The gang rigged the signal lights, stopped the train, failed to get an elderly driver to operate it, then forced conductor Jack Mills to drive on; he was beaten and later died of cancer, and the question of who struck him is disputed.

segments.title: Unloading the money and hiding at the farm
segments.summary: The gang unloaded the sacks of cash at Bridego Bridge and fled to Leatherslade Farm, where they stayed for about a week playing Monopoly with real money and leaving evidence behind; a neighbor reported them.

segments.title: Police investigation, informant, and arrests
segments.summary: Scotland Yard's Flying Squad under Tommy Butler tracked the gang, an informant named Mickey Keiho was reported to have named names, and members were arrested one by one, including a rooftop chase.

segments.title: Trials, sentencing, and wrongful convictions
segments.summary: The trial featured fingerprint and paint evidence, Biggs was tried separately, Roger Cordrey pleaded guilty, Bull received fourteen years despite apparently having little involvement, and judge Edmund Davies handed out heavy sentences.

segments.title: Escapes, Ronald Biggs in Brazil, and aftermath
segments.summary: Several robbers escaped prison; Biggs had plastic surgery, fled to Australia and then Brazil, avoided extradition due to a Brazilian child, was pursued by Jack Slipper, and later returned to Britain. The hosts cover the fate of the other robbers and the failed bank-note reissue idea.
